Abstract
We present a calculation of the coupling constants in the massive spin-1 ﬁeld chiral
Lagrangian to chiral O(p3) in the context of the extended Nambu–Jona-Lasinio
model described in Ref.
[1].

blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content:
[]{#1 label="1"}

At low-energies the strong, electromagnetic and weak interactions of the lightest pseudoscalar mesons can be described by an effective chiral Lagrangian [@sw; @gl]. This Lagrangian depends on a number of coupling constants which are not fixed by symmetry requirements alone but are, in principle, determined by the dynamics of the underlying QCD theory. Recently, there have been attempts to derive the low-energy effective chiral action of QCD [@bbr; @ert] with and without the inclusion of the low-lying resonances. The anomalous sector

Here we are concerned with the imaginary part of the effective action. The lowest order Lagrangian in the abnormal intrinsic parity sector describing the interaction of pseudoscalar mesons and external $l_\mu$ and $r_\mu$ sources is the one given by the Wess-Zumino (WZ) effective action [@wz; @ew]. The ${\cal O} (p^6)$ imaginary part of the effective action has been obtained in Ref. [@bij2] in the mean-field approximation of the model we consider here. blocks.title: Phenomenological applications
blocks.content:
[]{#5 label="5"}

In this Section we shall discuss some phenomenological applications from our calculations. In the whole following analysis we shall work in the chiral limit, *i.e.* ${\cal M} \to 0$. Therefore, we shall disregard possible $\omega_8-\rho^0$ and $\eta_8-\pi^0$ mixings, which are proportional to light-quark masses. In addition, the operators that generate these mixings are order ${\cal O} (p^4)$ in the chiral expansion [@gl2]. blocks.title: Vector resonance decays
Conclusions
blocks.content:
[]{#6 label="6"}

In this work we have studied in the context of the ENJL cut-off model considered in Ref. [@bbr] the anomalous and non-anomalous sectors of the chiral Lagrangian for spin-1 particles to ${\cal O}(p^3)$, including terms with two spin-1 particles. In this model, spin-1 particles are introduced not as gauge fields, in contrast to models in Refs. [@ban]-[@meis], but as fields which transform homogeneously.
